proposals.announcement_evidence: Joint Direct Attack Munition (JDAM) technical support and integration
proposals.rationale: The program name is unambiguous and the index carries it on ammunition-procurement BLI 353620, but the award is an IDIQ ceiling action for technical support and integration - 'studies and analysis; product improvement and upgrades; integration including, but not limited to, software integration and aircraft integration; and associated hardware and testing' - with no funds obligated and no appropriation named. That is development/engineering work of exactly the kind lens A flags when it is attached to a procurement line, so the evidence does not establish that the JDAM procurement BLI's own work was paid for here. Not linked.

proposals.announcement_evidence: F-15 Radar Modernization program (RMP) radar upgrades
proposals.rationale: A naive matcher fires here because 'Radar Modernization Program (RMP)' is a name this org's index carries twice - B05200 (B-52) and 0101113F (B-52 Squadrons) - but the announcement's RMP is the F-15 APG-82 radar upgrade (13 Group A kits, 13 Group B kits, 38 installs, conformal fuel tank installs, Boeing St. Louis, AFLCMC Wright-Patterson). proposals.announcement_evidence: Next Generation Overhead Persistent Infrared Polar Space Vehicles 1 and 2
proposals.rationale: The announcement spells out in full the abbreviation the index row abbreviates: 'Next Generation Overhead Persistent Infrared Polar' is Next-Gen OPIR Polar, and the award is for Space Vehicles 1 and 2 of that constellation - the NGP space segment itself, not a platform the contract merely supports. Northrop Grumman Space Systems Division at Redondo Beach is the NGP space-vehicle prime, and the money color matches the line exactly: 'Fiscal 2024 research and development funds in the amount of $93,832,830 are being obligated', against RDT&E Space Force PE 1206444SF. The index's sibling Next-Gen OPIR rows are the GEO segment (1206443SF), the ground segment (1206440SF) and the SMI (1206442SF); only 1206444SF owns Polar, so the name does not collide within the org. Building the Polar space vehicles is this PE's own work.

refute_a.reason: RDT&E money on an RDT&E line: the announcement obligates fiscal 2024 research and development funds and the lake's accounts for FA8810-18-C-0006 (057-3600;057-3620) intersect 1206444SF's 3620F; building Polar Space Vehicles 1 and 2 is the Next-Gen OPIR -- Polar line's own work, not support for a platform, and the title is no rollup.

refute_b.reason: Not refuted: 'Next-Gen OPIR Polar (NGP)' is owned by exactly one key in the index (1206444SF, doc 417); the sibling Next-Gen OPIR rows are Ground (1206440SF), SMI (1206442SF) and GEO (1206443SF), and the other 'Polar' rows (1206432SF, Enhanced Polar System / Polar MILSATCOM) are a satellite-communications line, not an infrared one. The only other '(NGP)' in the index is Next Generation Penetrator (0604327F), and the announcement spells the abbreviation out in full — 'Next Generation Overhead Persistent Infrared Polar Space Vehicles 1 and 2' — so the acronym collision cannot claim it. The alias is a literal expansion, not an invention, and the evidence is the work description, not the contractor name.

proposals.announcement_evidence: StormBreaker Production All Up Rounds and Containers for the U.S. Air Force
proposals.rationale: StormBreaker is the Air Force's own name for the GBU-53/B Small Diameter Bomb II - the sibling record 17 on this same contract (FA8672-21-C-0005) writes it out as 'StormBreaker (SDBII, GBU-53/B)', confirming the alias from the announcement corpus itself rather than from outside knowledge. The award buys production all up rounds and containers, i.e. the munitions the SDB002 procurement line exists to buy, not support for a platform that carries them; Raytheon Tucson is the SDB II prime and AFLCMC Eglin the SDB II contracting activity. Funds are procurement ('Fiscal 2022 U.S. Air Force Weapons Procurement funding in the amount of $92,908,493 was obligated'), matching procurement BLI SDB002 'SMALL DIAMETER BOMB II'. The RDT&E row 0207327F also carries 'GBU-53', but procurement money buying production rounds belongs to the procurement line, so SDB002 is the one proposed.

refute_a.reason: Procurement action against a procurement line: the lake records 057-3020 (Missile Procurement, AF) as the sole funding account on FA8672-21-C-0005, matching SDB002's 3020F, so the announcement's loose 'Weapons Procurement' wording names that same appropriation; production all up rounds and containers are the SMALL DIAMETER BOMB II line's own end item, not a platform it merely supports.

refute_b.reason: Not refuted, though the collision is real: 'GBU-53' is carried by two keys, 0207327F (doc 412 RDT&E, with 'SDB Increment II') and SDB002 (doc 410 procurement). The announcement's own words break the tie — 'StormBreaker Production All Up Rounds and Containers' bought with 'U.S. Air Force Weapons Procurement funding' is production hardware on a procurement line, not development on the RDT&E twin. The StormBreaker alias is not invented from outside knowledge: record 17 on this same contract writes 'StormBreaker (SDBII, GBU-53/B)'. Increment is right too — the other SDB key, SDB000, is the GBU-39 SDB I line. (The 'Weapons Procurement' wording versus doc 410 Missile Procurement is a money-color question for lens A, not an identity one.)

proposals.announcement_evidence: StormBreaker (SDBII, GBU-53/B) production all up rounds and containers
proposals.rationale: The announcement prints the designator itself - 'GBU-53/B' - which normalizes to the index row's 'GBU-53' on procurement BLI SDB002 'SMALL DIAMETER BOMB II', and it names SDB II in the same parenthesis, so identity is not in doubt. proposals.rationale: AGM-158C is the type designator of the Long Range Anti-Ship Missile, and the index puts that designator on BLI LRASM0, whose own title is LRASM - so the alias is the program's designator and its acronym, not a loose resemblance. refute_a.reason: The announcement names no appropriation, but the lake's accounts for FA8682-17-C-0037 (017-1507;057-3020;057-3600) contain 057-3020, which matches LRASM0's 3020F, so Air Force missile procurement money is genuinely on this award; Lot 1 production of 23 LRASM missiles is the line's own end item and LRASM0 is neither a rollup nor a catch-all title.

AGM-158C is LRASM's real type designator, so the alias is not invented, and the evidence is the work description ('long-range anti-ship missile (LRASM) Lot 1 production', 23 missiles), not the contractor's name. Lot 1 is not a distinct variant the index splits out. Flag for lens A, not for me: this announcement states no appropriation at all ('Fiscal ... funds' is absent), so the procurement-line placement rests on the work description alone.

proposals.announcement_evidence: the operation, maintenance, and sustainment of the Air Force's Launch and Test Range System

Not linked.

refute_a.reason: The award's money is not this line's appropriation: all 76 lake transactions on FA8730-21-C-0022, FY2021 through FY2026 and including the FY2023 actions this announcement covers, carry federal account 057-3600 (RDT&E, Air Force) and never 057-3080, so the award's accounts are disjoint from 833060's Other Procurement line (3080F) and load_announcement_links.money_color_ok would skip the link outright; the announcement's 'other procurement funds' phrase is contradicted by the contract's own funding record, and the RDT&E twin 0207455F is the line this action executes.

refute_b.reason: Not refuted: the name is owned by two keys — 833060 (doc 411, '3D Expeditionary Long-Range Radar') and 0207455F (doc 412 RDT&E, rows 'Three Dimensional Expeditionary Long Range Radar', 'AN/TPY-4', 'TPY-4') — but the announcement itself names the appropriation that separates them: 'Fiscal 2023 other procurement funds in the amount of $84,938,768 are being obligated', and Other Procurement AF is doc 411. Combined with what is bought (an option for four production radars plus production management and data), the same evidence does not attach equally well to the RDT&E twin. No variant question: AN/TPY-4 is 3DELRR under its nomenclature, and the evidence is the work description rather than the contractor name.

proposals.announcement_evidence: Shared Early Warning System support (SEWS)
proposals.rationale: The name matches the index row on SPCMOD exactly and the system is specific rather than generic, but the task order is characterised as 'sustainment and operations, maintenance and support of the SEWS System' - depot and organizational-level maintenance, configuration management, familiarization training, 24-hour troubleshooting, emergency maintenance - and SPCMOD is a Space Mods procurement rollup that the index shows carrying several unrelated names (UEWR, DREX). The announcement names no appropriation. A sustainment-and-operations task order hung on a modifications rollup is the lens-A failure mode, and the rubric says publish the smaller true number. Not linked.

proposals.announcement_evidence: MQ-9 Aircrew Training Support
proposals.rationale: §3 rejects this twice over. The MQ-9 is the platform the contract supports, not the program the PE funds, and the deliverable is generic training services - 'personnel, equipment, tools, materials, supervision... aircrew academic instruction; courseware development; and air and ground intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance test and training support' at Holloman, Creech and March. Nothing here executes the MQ-9 UAV development line's own work.

A purchase paid for entirely by a foreign customer does not pay for the U.S. JDAM procurement line's own work, which is what a published link would assert, so the §1 standard is not met even though the naming is unimpeachable. Not linked.

proposals.announcement_evidence: the joint primary aircraft training system T-6A/B Texan II Aircraft
proposals.rationale: The JPATS name appears in the text, but §3 rejects the award on two listed patterns: it is generic logistics services - 'Contractor Operated and Maintained Base Supply non-personal services' - and JPATS/the T-6 is the platform those supply services support, not the program the RDT&E line 0604233F (Specialized Undergraduate Flight Training) funds. proposals.announcement_evidence: the U.K. MQ-9B Protector program

The design, development and integration being bought adds capability to the U.K. baseline, not to the U.S. MQ-9 UAV line. The index's E-4B names all sit on RDT&E PE 0302015F, so this is O&M depot maintenance proposed against an RDT&E line - §3 generic services plus the lens-A appropriation failure mode.

proposals.announcement_evidence: the United Kingdom MQ-9B Protector program
proposals.rationale: The same U.K. Protector contract as record 53, one modification later, and rejected identically: 'This modification involves 100 percent Foreign Military Sales (FMS) to the United Kingdom.' The MQ-9B Protector is a British variant developed with British money; adding capability to that baseline is not the U.S. MQ-9 UAV program element's own work.

proposals.announcement_evidence: E-4B sustainment support
proposals.rationale: The order's own description is sustainment - 'The order will provide contractor logistic support services' - funded from 'Fiscal 2019 operations and maintenance funds in the amount of $57,188,079'. §3 rejects contractor logistic support as generic services, and the only E-4B names in the index belong to RDT&E PE 0302015F (Aircraft Modernization / NAOC), so an O&M sustainment order cannot be that line's own work.

proposals.announcement_evidence: Maui High Performance Computing Center (MHPCC) Support (VaCUUMS)
proposals.rationale: 'Maui' is the only shared term. The award is a University Affiliated Research Center IDIQ 'to establish or maintain an essential engineering, research, or development capability' supporting the Maui High Performance Computing Center - a DoD supercomputing facility - while the indexed name is the Maui Space Surveillance System, the optical telescope site on Haleakala. §3 rejects the award independently as a generic capability/research-support IDIQ with no named program, and the name collides across two PEs in this index (0603444F and 1206616SF) besides.
